title: A Case to Review the Model of Estate Management for Public Housing in Singapore
what_it_is: A Case to Review the Model of Estate Management for Public Housing in Singapore

sections.label: Town Councils manage common property
sections.summary: Since 1989, the Town Councils Act vested responsibility to manage, maintain and improve common property in the respective Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Since 1989, with the enactment of the Town Councils Act, the responsibility to manage, maintain and improve common property was vested in the respective Town Councils.

sections.label: Grant rates by flat size
sections.summary: The grant is $33.70 per month for 1-roomers, $26.20 for 2-roomers, $17 for 3-roomers and $9 for 4-roomers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Currently, the grant stands at $33.70 per month for 1-roomers; $26.20 per month for 2-roomers; $17 per month for 3-roomers and, finally, $9 per month for 4-roomers.

sections.label: Town Council estate management model
sections.summary: The current model of estate management through Town Councils has been in force for 32 years without much change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The current model of estate management through Town Councils has been in force for 32 years without much change.

sections.label: Tall skyscrapers in mature estates
sections.summary: Many of these projects are in mature estates and are usually 35 to 40 storeys high to optimise land usage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A good number of these projects may be found in mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They are, usually, much taller skyscrapers of between 35 and 40 storeys high, so as to optimise the usage of the land.

sections.label: Skyscraper maintenance costs higher
sections.summary: Maintenance costs for these skyscrapers are significantly higher than maintenance costs for the older housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The reality is maintenance costs for these skyscrapers are significantly higher than maintenance costs for the older housing estates.

sections.label: UK-made paver damages car tyres
sections.summary: The paver was made in the UK, looks beautiful on completion, and many have already damaged car tyres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Just do not throw it at anyone, especially in my direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: This paver was made in the UK – truly "enhanced" and unique!

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Without a doubt, they look beautiful on completion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: And, indeed, many have already damaged car tyres.

sections.label: Cross-subsidisation of BTO flats
sections.summary: Flat owners in older HDB estates may cross-subsidise residents in BTO flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The second problem is the potential for cross-subsidisation by flat owners from older HDB housing estates for residents in BTO flats.

sections.label: CIPC funding from Town Councils
sections.summary: 10% of CIPC funding comes from Town Council revenues, mostly S&CC from residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The problem, however, is that 10% of the CIPC funding comes from Town Council revenues, the bulk of it is S&CC from residents.

sections.label: Town Councils and infrastructure works
sections.summary: Town Councils should not undertake infrastructure-related works unless fully funded by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Respectfully, I suggest that Town Councils should not be undertaking these infrastructure-related works, which, by the way, are not cheap, unless they are fully funded by the Government.

sections.label: Centralisation of HDB maintenance services
sections.summary: There is merit in relooking at centralisation of resources with HDB to conduct maintenance services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: First, on the latter point, I think that there is merit in relooking at centralisation of resources again with HDB to conduct maintenance services.

sections.label: Maintenance costs and S&CC increases
sections.summary: Maintenance costs have risen faster than revenue, so other cost reductions must be exhausted before increasing S&CC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Already, with Progressive Wage Models implemented for cleaning jobs, maintenance costs have increased at a faster pace than revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: We need to exhaust all other ways to reduce costs before making the decision to increase S&CC.

sections.label: Town Council funding and responsibilities
sections.summary: Town Councils can retain project work, but funding models and S&CC grant criteria should be relooked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: On the second point of local community and identity, the Town Councils can retain the responsibility to take up project work, such as NRP, CIPC, ROS and so on, which, usually, involve deep consultations with residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Alternatively, if it is felt that the responsibility should still be sited with the Town Council, I think there is merit to relook at the funding models, in particular, the criteria for S&CC grants, and ensuring that S&CC by residents are not used for renewal of infrastructure and dealing with design issues in BTO developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: This allows us to retain the political accountability for Members of Parliament in reflecting the residents' concerns and preferences relating to their homes and public spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I have argued for a new model, which retains all the three main features of the 1989 Town Councils Act, while closing some of its current operational gaps.

sections.label: Town Council grants and rebates
sections.summary: In FY2020 the Government gave $146 million in operating grants and about $132 million in S&CC rebates, against $770 million in residential S&CC collection.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In FY2020, the Government provided $146 million in operating grants to Town Councils.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In addition, the Government also provides about $132 million worth of S&CC rebates, tiered according to flat type, to help residents pay for their S&CC.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This compares against a total S&CC collection of $770 million from residential units for that year.

sections.label: HDB replacing ineffective pavers
sections.summary: After Town Council feedback, HDB found the pavers' interlocking effect less effective than typical tiles and will replace them, bearing the full cost.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: While HDB had tested the pavers for durability prior to approving their usage, following feedback from the Town Council, HDB investigated and found the profile and interlocking effect of these pavers to be not as effective as the typical interlocking tiles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Hence, HDB will be replacing the pavers and bearing the costs fully.

sections.label: Town Council funds apportionment
sections.summary: Town Councils must apportion at least 40% of their income to these funds, and a similar percentage of Government grants goes to them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Town Councils have to apportion at least 40% of their income to these funds and a similar percentage of Government grants are also channelled to these funds.

sections.label: Government grants to Town Councils
sections.summary: The Government says it is committed to working with Town Councils on long-term financial sustainability, providing about $1.2 billion over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Government is committed to continue to work with Town Councils to ensure their long-term financial sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We provide substantial grants to Town Councils, with Government funding amounting to about $1.2 billion over the last five years.

sections.label: S&CC rates and cost increases
sections.summary: Town Councils have full autonomy to set S&CC rates, including differentiated rates, while MND may consider measures to cushion rising costs for residents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: These inflationary pressures affect all sectors, including the Government, which also has to manage a tight fiscal situation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Hence, the solution cannot simply be for the Government to take over estate management or to fully fund cost increases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Town Councils, being responsible for estate maintenance, play an important role in managing cost increases and apportioning costs among different households.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This is why Town Councils have the full autonomy to set S&CC rates, including differentiated rates, to achieve both financial sustainability and equity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: MND will be open to considering appropriate further measures, if necessary, to cushion the impact of rising costs on residents, especially those in greater need of help.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will also review the structure of S&CC operating grants regularly to ensure that it reflects the profile of our public housing stock, subject to the Government's fiscal position.
